output.brief: The rise in VA-220 failures traces to Pellacott's 2026-built valves, not to the new installers or the firmware. The lab's matched data shows Pellacott 2026 valves fail at the same rate (about 41 per 1,000) for legacy and new installers and on firmware 4.1 and 4.2. Durrant-Hale valves stay low in every group. Warehouse valves that were never installed leak at the seat in 11% of Pellacott 2026 lots. The independent calibration visit found the leak rig out of service since January, with no VA-220 test program on any other rig. Certificate tables repeat four fixed sequences, some already present in November 2025. So the certificates very likely do not reflect real tests, and the score rise came from complete-looking paperwork. I'm quite confident of this. Still unknown: whether the cause is the Corlin seal or the Line 3 move (they can't be separated), and whether other suppliers' records are also unreliable. Next steps: do not release the six held lots on new certificates. Quarantine 2026-built Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and retest with Brenmoor's own helium test. Drop the installer remediation plan. Require rig logs or witnessed tests in scoring, and check other suppliers' records soon.
